title: Back-Door Bounce Pass Timing
description: Pairs rehearse the exact moment of the back-door pass: the cutter plants, the passer fakes, and the bounce pass arrives as the cutter turns to the rim.

content.objective: Time the back-door bounce pass to the moment the cutter turns to the rim, so the catch happens in stride for a lay-up.
content.setup: Passer at the top of the key; cutter at the wing; a cone or coach as the denying defender.
content.organization: Rotate passer and cutter; alternate sides.
instructions: The cutter jogs out toward the wing as if to receive.
The cutter plants the outside foot and turns to the rim.
As the cutter turns, the passer fakes a pass to the wing, then bounce-passes to the space in front of the cutter.
The cutter catches in stride and finishes.
coachingPoints: Pass on the plant, not after it.
Bounce the ball just inside the lane.
Cutter shows a hand toward the rim.
commonMistakes: Late pass that arrives behind the cutter.
Chest pass into the defender's hands.
Cutter rounding the cut instead of planting.
content.safety: Cutters finish and clear the lane before the next rep.
progressions: Back door from the corner along the baseline.
variations: Back door off a dribble entry instead of a pass fake.
successCriteria: Cutter catches in stride on 8 of 10 reps.
content.gameApplication: Back-door cuts punish over-denial; they only work if the pass arrives on time.
